On Wed, 3 Mar 2027 at 08:22, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Amelia — thanks for sending these and for the clear summary. Copying Rishi (legal) and Lauren (CS/ops) to coordinate.

Thanks — I reviewed the PDF redlines and annotated them. Attaching an annotated DPA with comments. High-level reactions (so we can prioritize on the call):

1) Roles & legal basis: Redwood confirms we act as a processor for customer-provided personal data under the MSA/Order Form. We will accept a processor role statement in the DPA, but we cannot accept language that recharacterizes Redwood as a joint controller for general product telemetry. We can agree on narrow controller-controller collaboration language where required for CX or fraud investigations.

2) SCCs & TIA: We typically implement the EU Commission SCCs for processor-to-controller transfers and include a Transfer Impact Addendum for customers subject to elevated scrutiny. We will ask MedWellCare to confirm whether they require the UK addendum in addition to EU SCCs for UK-resident data.

3) Subprocessors: We maintain a public subprocessors list and will provide a snapshot. Customer approval is typically via notification with a short objection window, unless the subprocessor processes uniquely sensitive categories — in that case we can discuss contract-level controls.

4) Audit rights / security assessments: We can offer scoped audit rights (on-site vs. remote) with reasonable notice (30 days) and a mutually-agreed redaction process. We cannot accept open-ended unilateral audit provisions.

5) Retention & logs: We will propose retention language aligned with operational needs and data minimization; for aggregate operational logs 2–7 years is negotiable; for customer content we prefer deletion at termination with limited backups window.

6) Liability / caps: Any departure from standard caps will need commercial approval (deal desk). Please surface what cap MedWellCare legal is expecting.

7) Security measures: We'll include a brief security exhibit linking to our SOC2 report and the security controls summary. We'll discuss whether encrypted-at-rest region restrictions (AWS EU only) are required and whether that must be contractual or operational.

Next steps for the call: confirm time, I'll walk through the annotated DPA and highlight which items are legal vs. product/ops decisions.

Thanks, Rishi and team. Thu 4 Mar didn't work for our internal reviewers; the Thu afternoon slot was tight so we took Fri to finish internal review.

A few clarifications ahead of the call:
- We appreciate the confirmation on processor role. We can accept processor language for product data; we'll flag telemetry separately.
- For transfers: MedWellCare requires EU Commission SCCs + a short Transfer Impact Addendum. We also need the contract to explicitly state that data will be stored in AWS EU regions for EU customer data; please confirm whether you can contractually commit to AWS EU-only storage for MedWellCare workload (we understand some cached tokens may transit other regions).
- On subprocessors: please share the latest snapshot and confirm whether any third-party embeddings/feature stores are used that store token-level content long-term.
- Liability: our counsel is proposing a carve-out for wilful misconduct and a cap consistent with PO value. We'll surface a target cap for Rishi to review before final.

We're happy to proceed with a 30-min walkthrough next Tue 9 Mar 10:00 CET if that works for Redwood. Please send a calendar invite and include the technical contact for any operational Qs (Lauren?).

DocuSign: once DPA language is agreed we will push the DPA + Order Form via DocuSign (link attached).

Best,
Amelia
